source_checks: All four changed files rehashed and exact reverse patch recovers each pinned preimage. No GPU shader, command emitter, rd_flush CACHE_FLUSH_TS/CP_WAIT_REG_MEM, WFI, or per-EXEC resource cap change.

Radish physical initialization explicitly requires DRM driver name msm. Runtime FD_VERSION_SOFTPIN gate matches msm_pipe selection of sp_funcs; no legacy/virtio private-struct cast. This is matched-monorepo private coupling, not a general cross-version ABI promise.

fd_submit_flush finalizes command buffers and queues the worker. fd_fence_flush executes pipe flush and waits util_queue ready. MSM worker finishes BO/cmd table construction, ioctl, error/fence fields and local temporary arrays before signaling readiness. Later cleanup only releases its submit reference; retained caller submit/ring references prevent table/slab destruction. No later command construction touches that submit. Shared BO idx/fence fields may change under their existing protocols; footprint does not read mutable idx/fence fields.

fd_submit_new owns one caller submit reference; primary registration owns an additional ring reference, caller owns one ring reference; fd_submit_flush returns an owned fence. Window keeps all three until same-pipe latest completion, then releases each once; submit destruction releases primary and BO references. CS backing pointer is nonowning but kept alive by ring and submit BO references.

Each enqueue is flushed to the same MSM submit queue before later enqueue; all previous GPU cache/WFI boundaries remain. Waiting newest successfully enqueued fence therefore covers earlier accepted same-queue work. Queuing up to64 chunks is queue depth, not simultaneous64 workgroups; unchanged per-EXEC thread/shared/register guard remains.

V2 initializes appended internal submit_error to -EINPROGRESS at the sole allocation site, records exact MSM ioctl return before readiness, and rejects nonzero after fd_fence_flush before window admission. Earlier accepted window is drained on failed current enqueue; Vulkan completion signals are skipped. No kernel-fence-zero or wrap assumption. A nonzero ioctl report is not asserted to imply no kernel acceptance; existing kernel GEM ownership/device-lost cleanup policy applies to that exceptional case.

All non-dispatch commands, indirect CPU argument reads, sampling/unsupported pipelines drain before CPU preparation. No-sampling eligible path returns immediately in rd_prepare_sampling. Profiling disables deferred completion and retains original sample lifetime. Zero-size dispatch can leave prior window for the later final drain without reading data.

Final drain precedes vk_sync_signal_many. Dispatch allocation/validation failures flow through queue error drain. Oversize/segmented or new CS-parent-budget failures drain prior work and wait the current fence before release. No accepted partial batch or extra unbounded pending slot is retained.
